report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. Rigorous clinical trials and real-world data demonstrate that the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, trade name Shingrix) substantially reduces the risk of shingles (herpes zoster) in adults aged 70 years or older.

**Evidence Summary:**
1. **Pivotal Clinical Trial (ZOE-70):** In the landmark Phase 3 ZOE-70 randomized controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine*, RZV demonstrated a **91.3% vaccine efficacy** against shingles in adults aged 70 and older. High efficacy was maintained across sub-groups aged 70–79 (90.0%) and 80 years or older (91.4%).
2. **CDC Recommendations:** The Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend RZV for adults aged 50 and older—including adults 70+—due to its efficacy in preventing shingles and postherpetic neuralgia.
3. **Real-World Effectiveness:** Post-licensure claims-based cohort studies and observational analyses confirm that RZV achieves high real-world effectiveness against herpes zoster among older adult populations, mirroring the results seen in clinical trials.

The claim that the vaccine reduces shingles in adults aged 70 or older is firmly backed by high-quality scientific evidence.

**Sources:**
* https://www.nejm.org/doi/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800?page=2
* https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/67/wr/mm6703a5.htm
* https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8442779/
* https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7336348/
